summary.headline: Paper pages carry real, well-formed citation metadata (Highwire Press meta tags) but nothing in schema.org form -- machine-readable for citation tools, invisible to schema.org-only consumers — medium severity, Add a ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD block to paper pages, generated from the same values already populating the citation_* meta tags, without removing the existing tags.

findings.title: Paper pages carry real, well-formed citation metadata (Highwire Press meta tags) but nothing in schema.org form -- machine-readable for citation tools, invisible to schema.org-only consumers
findings.evidence: All 8 sampled /abs/<id> paper pages carry a complete, correctly-populated set of Highwire Press citation meta tags -- citation_title, citation_author (repeated per author), citation_date, citation_online_date, citation_pdf_url, citation_arxiv_id, citation_abstract -- a real, well-established machine-readable format that Google Scholar, Zotero, Mendeley and similar citation tools already consume. None of the 15 sampled pages (including these 8) contain any schema.org JSON-LD, microdata, or RDFa. This is a materially different, milder situation than a site with no machine-readable metadata at all: the facts are genuinely machine-extractable today, just via a citation-specific vocabulary rather than schema.org's ScholarlyArticle/Dataset types, which is what a general-purpose AI assistant extracting facts via schema.org specifically would look for.

reproduction.command: curl -s https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00440 | grep -o 'name="citation_[a-z_]*"' | sort -u; curl -s https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.00440 | grep -c 'application/ld+json'
reproduction.observed: citation_* meta tags present (title, author x4, date, pdf_url, arxiv_id, abstract); 0 application/ld+json blocks
reproduction.expected: A ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD block (headline, author, datePublished, identifier) alongside the existing citation_* tags, not instead of them

suggested_action.summary: Add a ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD block to paper pages, generated from the same values already populating the citation_* meta tags, without removing the existing tags.
suggested_action.mechanism: The citation_* tags and schema.org serve different, non-overlapping consumer ecosystems -- academic citation tools versus general-purpose schema.org-consuming systems. Since every needed value (title, authors, date, arxiv id, abstract) already exists in the citation_* tags, emitting the same values a second time as ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD closes the schema.org gap without touching the existing, functioning citation metadata.
steps: Add a ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD block per paper page with headline, author (name per author), datePublished, and identifier (the arXiv id), sourced from the same data already feeding the citation_* tags.

opportunities.title: Publish an llms.txt at the platform level pointing at how to query the API/OAI-PMH interface for bulk or structured access
opportunities.rationale: arXiv already exposes a real bulk-metadata interface (referenced in its own robots.txt disallow list, e.g. /oai2), but a retrieval-capable assistant arriving via ordinary crawling has no way to discover that a better, structured access path exists for large-scale or precise queries.
opportunities.mechanism: Pointing assistants at the proper API/metadata interface, rather than leaving them to scrape abstract pages one at a time, is both more efficient for arXiv's own infrastructure and more reliable for the assistant.
steps: Add an llms.txt at the site root naming the arXiv API and its documentation as the preferred bulk/structured access path.

not_assessed.reason: This run's sample focused on category-listing and individual paper pages to properly exercise the research content pattern; arXiv's own /about or /help pages were not sampled.
not_assessed.impact: Cannot confirm whether the platform itself (as distinct from individual papers) carries Organization-level identity markup.

not_assessed.impact: Not applicable in the usual sense for this site type -- arXiv's own submissions are the primary source for most of its content -- but genuinely not checked.

not_assessed.check: Question-coverage probe (answerability-audit, check 1) across arXiv's full breadth
not_assessed.reason: Only 4 of arXiv's roughly 150 subject categories were sampled (cs.HC, astro-ph, math.CT, q-fin.PR, q-bio.GN), chosen for topical diversity rather than exhaustive coverage.
not_assessed.impact: Findings should be read as representative of the shared page templates (which are identical across categories) rather than as claims about every subject area's specific content.
